label: First widget
title: Your first widget
description: Create a counter, preview your changes and import it into OverCrow.

blocks.html:
1. Download the kit

Install Node.js 22 or later, then download and extract the kit. Open a terminal in the extracted overcrow-creator-kit.

Download the creator kit ↓

Prefer to edit online? Use the Studio and download your project or package when ready.

2. Create a counter

blocks.title: Terminal · Windows or Linux
blocks.source:
node overcrow.mjs init my-widget
cd my-widget
npm run dev

blocks.html:
Open the URL printed in the terminal and click +1. This browser preview reloads valid edits; an error leaves the last working version visible.

3. Make a change

Change colors in widget/styles.css or labels in widget/locales/en.mjs and widget/locales/fr.mjs. widget/index.html controls the layout.

To add two on each click, replace the existing increment() function in widget/view.js with:

blocks.title: widget/view.js · increment()

blocks.html:
Change the button label from +1 to +2 in widget/index.html.

4. Build a package

Stop the preview with Ctrl+C, then run:

blocks.title: From my-widget/
blocks.source:
npm run check
npm run package

blocks.html:
The terminal prints the .ocpkg path under .overcrow-output/. It contains the files in widget/.

5. Test in OverCrow

Import the package in Control Center, review its permissions and activate it from the overlay library. In a game, test clicks, resizing and hiding/showing the widget.

For an update, increase version in widget/manifest.json, then package and import again.

Next steps

Save preferences, call an API or try another example. The creator kit guide covers preview controls, native testing and PowerShell troubleshooting.

label: Installation
title: Installation
description: Get the creator kit, the SDK and OverCrow.

blocks.html:
Start with the kit

The creator kit includes the SDK, templates and local tools. Install Node.js 22+ and follow Your first widget.

Download the SDK

For an existing project, download overcrow.js, the TypeScript declarations and the MIT license. The example archives already include them.

Write JavaScript directly or compile TypeScript with your own tools. Ship the resulting static files; the .d.ts file supplies editor types.

System requirements

TaskLinuxWindows
Create, preview and packageNode.js 22+Node.js 22+
Run a package in the overlayImport in Control CenterImport in Control Center
Native development and devtoolsInstalled CLI and Control Center for the same userCompatible OverCrow installation
Native development displayOffscreen; import a package to test in gameSame behavior

Linux : Hyprland 0.55+ Wayland, Plasma 6 Wayland, GNOME 46–50 Wayland or X11/EWMH.
Windows : Windows 10 1809+ or Windows 11 x64, with WebView2 and the application’s graphics prerequisites.

Use windowed or borderless games. Exclusive fullscreen is unsupported.

Install OverCrow

Download an official release. On Linux, check that the native CLI is available:

blocks.title: Linux terminal
blocks.source: command -v overcrow-widget

blocks.html:
If the command is missing, check the installed OverCrow package.

Import the SDK

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Load view.js with <script type="module" src="./view.js"></script>. Native services require OverCrow; the creator-kit browser preview simulates them.

Serve a plain HTML project

For a simple layout preview, serve the folder with your editor’s local server. With Python 3 installed, use:

blocks.title: Linux · optional static server
blocks.source: python3 -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1

blocks.title: Windows · Python launcher
blocks.source: py -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1

blocks.html:
Open http://127.0.0.1:4173/. Double-clicking index.html can block JavaScript modules on file:// URLs. This static server provides no native services.

See available native services.

label: Concepts
title: How a widget works
description: An HTML view, a manifest and an optional controller.

blocks.html:
The view

A widget starts with a local HTML page. Write its interface with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. OverCrow provides the frame, position and panel opacity. Keep the HTML/body background transparent and check small sizes.

An optional controller

Add a second HTML document when requests or cached state should survive a native view reload. The view sends messages to this controller; the controller replies with data to display. Use storage for data that must survive a full restart.

Controller · data⇄runtime.send⇄View · interface

See a counter with a controller.

The manifest

The manifest identifies your widget, names its files and declares permissions. OverCrow checks these permissions for network requests, storage, clipboard writes and game events. Read the manifest guide.

From project to package

StepResult
DevelopEdit files and preview your widget.
PrepareValidate the manifest and calculate file hashes.
DistributeExport a .ocpkg, test it in OverCrow and follow marketplace admission.

Use a framework

Any framework that produces local static files can work. Run its build yourself and ship scripts, styles, images, fonts and licenses in the widget. WASM can handle local computation. Keep bundles small and pause unnecessary work when hidden.

The runtime blocks remote images, iframes, Web Workers and audio/video media. A network permission enables overcrow.fetch requests only. Use SDK data or an authorized HTTPS API; game memory and native modules are outside the widget’s access.

label: Creator kit
title: Creator kit
description: Create, preview and package a widget on Windows or Linux.

blocks.html:
Install Node.js 22+, then extract the kit. The source and download use the same revision as this documentation.

Download the creator kit ↓   Or use the online Studio →

Create a project

blocks.title: From the extracted kit folder
blocks.source:
node overcrow.mjs init my-widget --template counter --id com.example.my-widget
cd my-widget
npm run dev

blocks.html:
Choose blank for an empty view, counter to start or checklist for saved tasks. Omit --id to generate an ID. Existing folders are protected. Full tutorial.

Project files

blocks.title: Only widget/ is packaged
blocks.source:
my-widget/
  widget/             # HTML, CSS, JS, manifest and SDK
  preview.json        # Simulated data
  tooling/            # Local tools
  package.json        # Development commands
  .overcrow-output/   # Exported packages

blocks.html:
Keep API keys, personal fixtures and build tools outside widget/. Place your framework’s compiled static output there.

Edit Counter/Checklist labels in widget/locales/en.mjs and fr.mjs. i18n.mjs updates data-i18n elements and the page language; edit interactions in view.js.

In Studio, select/reset templates in the header and manage files in the explorer. Update imports after renaming. Download the project to keep browser drafts elsewhere; the ZIP preserves empty folders.

Commands

CommandResult
npm run devBrowser preview; reloads valid edits.
npm run checkValidate sources and manifest without changes.
npm run packageCalculate hashes and export to .overcrow-output/.
npm run dev -- --nativeNative session; keeps the controller during view reloads.
npm run doctorReport Node, OS and native host availability.

Ctrl+C stops a session. For another preview port: npm run dev -- --port 4176.

Browser preview

Open the printed 127.0.0.1 URL. Simulate the session, language and overlay mode. Invalid edits keep the last valid view; permission changes require a restart.

  • The three-dot menu adjusts content scale (50–175%) and frame opacity (0–100%); starters use 100%. Use sliders or enter a percentage. Widget CSS backgrounds stay independent.
  • Drag the 22-pixel top strip to move. The starter’s lower-right handle resizes from its fixed upper-left corner. Arrow keys work when focused; Shift increases the step.
  • The eye controls passive visibility. Passive mode hides frame controls and updates SDK visibility and overlayMode. Close is illustrative. Escape or an outside click closes options.
  • Frame settings survive widget reloads until page refresh. OverCrow supplies this frame; keep it outside your widget.

Reload restarts view and controller. Legacy browser storage is separated by widget ID; use getItem/setItem instead of localStorage.myKey. SDK storage behavior.

Simulate data

blocks.title: preview.json · beside widget/

blocks.html:
Declare the matching HTTPS permission. Fixtures match exact method/URL, ignore request bodies and make no external request. Use text for text or status 503 for failure. Missing fixtures return fixture_missing. Named game events require replay.

Test the native engine

blocks.title: Windows and Linux
blocks.source:
npm run dev -- --native
npm run dev -- --native --devtools
npm run dev -- --native --replay ./events.json

blocks.html:
Linux requires Control Center and overcrow-widget; Windows requires a compatible installation. For a portable host, add --host "C:/Tools/OverCrow/OverCrow.exe".

The kit recalculates hashes and reloads valid views while retaining the controller. Restart after controller edits, expanded permissions or storage permission changes.

Offscreen session

Use devtools to inspect the native engine. Import a package to test overlay input, focus, capture and clipboard gestures.

Import your package

blocks.title: Create a .ocpkg
blocks.source: npm run package

blocks.html:
Import the printed path in Control Center, review permissions and activate the widget. Increase version in widget/manifest.json for each update. Hash suffixes preserve exports; they do not change the version.

Troubleshooting

If PowerShell blocks npm.ps1, use npm.cmd run dev or node tooling/overcrow.mjs dev.

blocks.title: Structured diagnostics
blocks.source: node tooling/overcrow.mjs check --json

blocks.html:
JSON reports ok, error code, field and action; failure exits nonzero. OverCrow and the marketplace perform final validation. Look up an error.

Native services and reference widgets.

label: Manifest
title: The manifest
description: Identify your widget and declare its files and permissions.

blocks.html:
Start with this manifest

This is enough for a local view. The kit generates file hashes when packaging.

blocks.title: widget/manifest.json · before packaging

blocks.html:
Keep id stable across updates: it identifies the widget’s installation and storage.

Fields

FieldMeaning
schemaVersionThe number 1.
apiVersionThe string "1", or "2" for native services and presentation.
idStable lowercase reverse-domain ID, such as com.example.my-widget.
versionWidget SemVer, such as 1.0.0; increase it for updates.
entrypoints.viewLocal HTML page to display.
entrypoints.controllerOptional local HTML controller.
permissionsThe network, events, storage, clipboard or native capabilities you need.
localizationLanguages you ship and the default locale.
presentationAPI v2 sizing and native options.
filesGenerated file sizes and SHA-256 hashes.

See API v2 native services and language declarations.

Allow an HTTPS request

blocks.title: Inside permissions

blocks.html:
Call overcrow.fetch with the declared origin, method and path. A trailing slash permits the path’s subtree; without it, only the exact path is allowed. Host wildcards, redirects and local destinations are rejected. Network reference.

Include your files

Put HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, translations and licenses in widget/. Use relative ASCII paths, with no .., links or case collisions. Keep build tools outside this folder.

The generated files must match every packaged file; the manifest excludes its own hash. The native CLI requires this ledger for dev and package. Unknown fields are rejected.

Review added permissions and restart development to accept them. Preparation never infers permissions from your code.

Limits

ItemLimit
Package128 MiB; 4,096 entries including the manifest
Manifest1 MiB
Paths192 ASCII bytes

See the relevant API pages for request limits, messages and languages.

label: Examples
title: Examples
description: Download a starting project or explore a native service.

blocks.html:
Blank · empty view

HTML, CSS, JavaScript and manifest, with the SDK and license. Add your own interface.

Download sources ↓   Edit in Studio →

Counter · first widget

A counter with two buttons. Learn layout and packaging with a view that uses no network or storage.

Download sources ↓   Edit in Studio →

Checklist · saved tasks

Add, check and remove tasks. Data is versioned and validated; invalid data is reported and preserved. Requests storage: true.

Download sources ↓   Edit in Studio →

Warframe Market · API and cache

Search a catalog, list buy/sell offers and copy a message. A controller manages requests and an IndexedDB cache. Permissions: GET to https://api.warframe.market/v2/, storage and clipboard writes.

Download sources ↓

Warframe Market is reference bundle 2.0.5, including its bundled SDK. Source history ↗.

Use a source archive

Create a creator-kit project, then copy the extracted files into its widget/. Choose your own ID and version, and keep MIT notices. You can also use the Linux native CLI.

These archives are sources. Package and import them to test rendering and interaction in OverCrow. Counter and Checklist are starter projects, not marketplace listings.

Native service examples

Each API v2 reference declares its required capabilities and includes English/French labels. Choose a service.
session · clock · performance · fps · stopwatch · media · notes · score · rating · reviews · journal · twitch

label: Network
title: Network requests
description: Read an HTTPS API with overcrow.fetch.

blocks.html:
Call overcrow.fetch

Pass a URL and optional request settings. The default method is GET.

blocks.title: Supported signature

blocks.html:
Declare the HTTPS origin, method and path prefix in the manifest.

Read a JSON response

blocks.title: view.js · requires GET /v2/ permission

blocks.html:
Read the result

MemberBehavior
status / okHTTP status; ok is true for 200–299.
contentTypeContent type or null.
bodyUsedTrue after the first body read.
json()Parse the body once; validate the returned data before using it.
text() / arrayBuffer()Read text or bytes once. A second body read rejects with body_used.

A 404 or 503 is an HTTP response: check response.ok. A denied permission or timeout rejects the call with an SDK error.

Limits and permissions

The host limits requests to 30 seconds, 2 MiB for request bodies and 32 MiB for response bodies. It rejects redirects, proxies and local destinations. Bodies are sent as bytes; a string does not automatically set a JSON Content-Type.

headers, signal, cookies and ambient authentication are unsupported. A Promise.race can stop your wait, but does not cancel the native request. Ignore replies from superseded searches.

Use overcrow.fetch for external requests. This permission does not enable remote images, WebSockets, workers or iframes. Keep API keys out of distributed files; use a service you control for private credentials.

Handle failed loads

Keep the last valid data during refresh, distinguish empty results from errors, show cache age and offer a retry. Warframe Market shows this with a controller and cache. Look up error codes.

label: Game session
title: Game session
description: Read session state and follow its changes.

blocks.html: Read the current session

blocks.title: Read once

blocks.html:
A snapshot contains the session data available from OverCrow. A missing game or sensor can leave values unavailable. Check the type before formatting; zero is a valid measurement.

Snapshot fields

FieldType / unit
running / selectedActiveGame/session activity booleans. A minimal snapshot may contain only running.
steamAppIdNumber or null; no title or artwork.
sessionElapsedMsSession duration in milliseconds, or null.
overlayMode"passive" or "interactive".
cpuPercentHundredthsProcess CPU in hundredths of a percent, or null.
residentBytesResident memory in bytes, or null.
cpuTemperatureMillicelsius / gpuTemperatureMillicelsiusThousandths of a Celsius degree, or null.

GameSnapshot describes these optional fields. Extra JSON fields are preserved; an invalid type in a known field rejects with invalid_response.

This snapshot has no FPS, inventory, health or player-position field. Use native services for features such as FPS, subject to host support.

Follow changes

blocks.title: Subscribe, then read the initial state

blocks.html:
onSnapshot delivers future changes. Read snapshot() for the initial state. Malformed events are ignored. The returned stop() function unsubscribes and is safe to call again.

Listen for named events

For an integration or replay that emits named events, declare them in permissions.gameEvents, then subscribe:

blocks.title: Example replay event

blocks.html:
The host or fixture must actually emit this name. Native snapshot changes use onSnapshot. A replay field such as elapsedMs is separate from the native sessionElapsedMs.

Test with a fixture

Replay ordered events to test your handlers without a game. Use OverCrow for actual game and sensor availability.
Explore other native services.

label: OverCrow services
title: Use OverCrow services
description: Display FPS, notes, media or Twitch chat using a shared set of SDK methods.

blocks.html:
Read data from OverCrow and add controls to your widget. Choose a service, then follow its example.

  • Performance and FPS
  • Stopwatch
  • Media
  • Notes and checklists
  • PlayerVox ratings and reviews
  • Session journal
  • Twitch chat

1. Declare permissions

Use apiVersion: "2" and list the required capabilities in permissions.capabilities. For example, displaying FPS requires fps.read:

blocks.title: manifest.json

blocks.html:
OverCrow asks the user to approve these permissions. New permissions need new consent, even when an account is already connected.

2. Display live data

onSnapshot() delivers the current state, then updates it. This example creates an FPS label; unavailable measurements display a dash.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Handle unavailable data

Each service returns { status, data, contextId, revision }. Only ready and stale can include data; individual measurements can still be null.

statusWhat to show
readyCurrent data.
staleOlder data, labelled with its age (sampleAgeMs).
unavailableA placeholder: no usable game session or measurement.
unsupportedAn explanation: this host or platform lacks the feature.
permissionDeniedA missing permission notice.
notConnectedA button to open the native connection screen.
rateLimitedWait before retrying; use retryAfterMs when provided.

For a one-off read, use snapshot() and catch errors. host.capabilities() reports supported and granted for each capability. Without OverCrow or a simulator, snapshot() rejects with bridge_unavailable; an initial subscription failure reports unavailable.

Keep at most 128 active subscriptions and 32 pending actions. Call the function returned by onSnapshot() when the view is disposed.

Find fields and units

Each service page describes its fields, units and limits. The TypeScript definitions provide the complete types. Treat missing values as unavailable, not zero.

Respond to a user action

Call controls directly from a click in an interactive view, before awaiting unrelated work. Each native gesture is short-lived and single-use. Editors and confirmations open in OverCrow; controller pages cannot trigger them. A result of accepted means opened or queued, not saved or sent. Follow the next snapshot to display the outcome.

For editing, pass the current revision as described on the service page. On conflict or stale_context, refresh the displayed data and let the user retry. Other action errors include capability_denied, permission_denied, unsupported_operation, unavailable and rate_limited. Never automatically repeat an uncertain write.

Size and display options

presentation.sizing.modeBehaviour
intrinsicFits the content; no manual resize.
autoHeightAutomatic height, adjustable width.
manualBoth dimensions can be resized.

Declare integer preferred, min and max dimensions in the manifest. Up to 16 boolean, enum or bounded number options can appear in the native menu. Read their values through presentation.onSnapshot(), in data.options.

For a view whose content is inside <main>, report its unscaled CSS size (integers from 1 to 4096):

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Apply this to your content element and group repeated size changes before reporting them. OverCrow owns position, resize, opacity, scale and passive visibility. See the reference manifests for complete display options.

Private data

Sensitive permissions cannot be combined with widget network access or raw clipboard writes. They also force temporary browser storage, even with storage: true. Account tokens and private API calls stay in OverCrow. Render user content as text and honour moderation/deletion updates.

Twitch connection and message composition · Storage policy

Try an example

The reference widgets use only the SDK. Browser previews use sample data; connection, editor and confirmation actions return cancelled. FPS are unsupported by default. Test these features and permissions in OverCrow before distributing your widget.

Existing API v1 widgets

API v1 remains supported. Replace overcrow.js and overcrow.d.ts together. Switch to apiVersion: "2" when adding capabilities or presentation settings. Keep the original behaviour of game.onSnapshot() (future updates only) and the original v1 CPU units; the new services use their own contracts.

label: Performance & FPS
title: Read CPU, memory, temperatures and FPS
description: Display available game measurements, with their units and freshness.

blocks.html:
Build a compact performance display with telemetry for CPU, memory and temperatures, plus a separate FPS service. A missing measurement is not zero.

Permissions

Merge these fields into your manifest. Use telemetry.read for system measurements and fps.read for frame rate; omit either permission if unused. Declaring them requests user consent and does not guarantee platform support.

blocks.title: manifest.json (fragment)

blocks.html:
Minimal example

Load this as a module in your view, with overcrow.js beside it. It creates two text labels. Each subscription reads the current value and then follows updates.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Units and availability

FieldMeaning
normalizedCpuPercentHundredths0–10000; divide by 100 for total-machine CPU percent.
residentBytesBytes; divide by 1048576 for MiB.
cpuTemperatureMillicelsius, gpuTemperatureMillicelsiusHost sensor temperatures; divide by 1000 for °C.
FPS value, sampleAgeMs, staleFrame rate, measurement age in milliseconds, and freshness.

Every measurement can be null, even when the service is ready. Keep a stale label and its age when showing old data; an absent age is unknown. A service marked unsupported has no provider on that host.

Linux CPU and memory cover the selected Steam process group or manually selected process descendants. Windows uses the validated target process. Temperatures describe host sensors, not the game process. Windows CPU temperature is unavailable; Windows FPS needs the validated capture service. Native Wayland currently has no FPS source.

The API v1 game.cpuPercentHundredths field keeps its original meaning; do not treat it as normalized CPU. Browser preview measurements are fictional and FPS defaults to unsupported.

Continue with shared service rules, the complete TypeScript definitions and the working reference widgets.

label: Stopwatch
title: Display and control the stopwatch
description: Read elapsed time and let the user start, pause or reset the native stopwatch.

blocks.html:
Use the native stopwatch when your widget needs elapsed time with start, pause and reset controls. OverCrow owns its state; your view displays that state.

Permissions

Merge these fields into your manifest. stopwatch.read is enough for this display-only example. The host must support and grant the requested capability.

blocks.title: manifest.json (fragment)

blocks.html:
Minimal example

This view module creates a time label. Put overcrow.js beside it. The subscription reads the current state and then follows updates.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Add a Start button

Add stopwatch.control to your manifest’s capabilities for this optional button module. It requests a native action when clicked and displays its result.

blocks.title: controls.js

blocks.html:
Time and controls

elapsedMs is elapsed time in milliseconds; running tells you whether the stopwatch is advancing. This small example shows the latest reported time. For a smoother display, you may add locally elapsed time while a ready snapshot says running, then resynchronize on every update. Never keep advancing a stale or unavailable value.

start(), pause() and reset() return an action result. They do not return a new stopwatch snapshot. Read the next subscription update to display the actual state. An accepted result means the command was queued, not that the displayed time has already changed.

Run controls from a user interaction and handle refusal, revoked permission or an unavailable session. The native host rechecks access. Do not automatically repeat a command after an uncertain result. The browser preview changes only its fictional stopwatch in memory.

Continue with shared service rules, the complete TypeScript definitions and the working reference widgets.

label: Media
title: Display the current track and playback controls
description: Read native media information and use the controls offered by the current player.

blocks.html:
Show the track exposed by the native media service and let the user control playback. The available buttons depend on what the current player supports.

Permissions

Merge these fields into your manifest. media.read reads track information; media.control enables playback commands. For a display-only widget, remove the control permission. These sensitive permissions require an empty network list and clipboardWrite: false.

blocks.title: manifest.json (fragment)

blocks.html:
Minimal example

This module creates track and status labels plus a play/pause button. Put overcrow.js beside it. The button stays disabled while data is missing or stale, or the player does not offer that action.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Track information and controls

title, artist and artworkHandle can be null. playbackState is playing, paused or stopped. Show text with textContent and clear the old track when data becomes unavailable.

actions.previous, actions.playPause and actions.next describe the player’s available controls. Call previous(), playPause() or next() from a user interaction. An available player action still needs the widget’s control permission. Handle errors and use subsequent snapshots for the resulting playback state; accepted only means queued.

An artwork handle is an opaque identifier, not an image URL. await overcrow.assets.read(handle) returns a local PNG Blob, at most 512 KiB. Create an object URL to display it, revoke that URL when replaced or closed, and discard a late image response if the track or context changed. Never replace the handle with an external URL.

Sensitive permissions force temporary browser data even when storage is requested. Native session/account changes discard that browser data. Preview playback controls affect fictional data only.

Continue with shared service rules, the complete TypeScript definitions and the working reference widgets.

label: Notes
title: Read notes and open the native editor
description: Display native notes and checklists, with revision checks for every change.

blocks.html:
Display the user’s native notes and checklists in your widget. OverCrow provides the text editor and deletion confirmation; your widget can also select notes and change checklist items.

Permissions

Merge these fields into your manifest. notes.read allows reading and selecting; notes.write allows creation, editing, deletion and checklist changes. These sensitive permissions prohibit network and clipboard access and force temporary browser data, even with storage requested.

blocks.title: manifest.json (fragment)

blocks.html:
Minimal example

This view module displays the active note and opens the native editor to create another. Put overcrow.js beside it. The button uses the latest ready document revision.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Actions and saving

requestCreate({expectedRevision}), requestEdit({noteId, expectedRevision}) and requestDelete({noteId, expectedRevision}) open native interfaces. The user enters text or confirms deletion there; these methods do not accept a note body.

select({noteId, expectedRevision}) selects a note with read permission. setChecked({noteId, itemId, checked, expectedRevision}) directly requests a checklist change with write permission. Take IDs from current data. For every notes action, use data.documentRevision, not the snapshot’s outer revision.

accepted means opened or queued, not saved. saveState reports accepted, saving, persisted, conflict or failed. Retain any local draft until durable confirmation. On a conflict, refresh the displayed state before the user tries again; never automatically replay an uncertain edit.

The document contains at most 8 notes and 64 checklist items per note. A note has an id, title, body and items; activeNoteId may be null. Render all text as text. Native notes stay in their own store when temporary browser data is cleared. Preview editors return cancelled; checklist actions only change fictional data.

Continue with shared service rules, the complete TypeScript definitions and the working reference widgets.

label: PlayerVox
title: Show scores, personal ratings and reviews
description: Read PlayerVox scores and reviews, or let the user edit their rating in OverCrow.

blocks.html:
Add the game’s community score, the user’s own rating or a page of player reviews. Start with the score: it needs one permission and no edit controls.

Permissions

Merge these fields into your manifest for the example. Request only the additional permissions your widget uses; declaring a permission does not grant it.

blocks.title: manifest.json (fragment)

blocks.html:
Minimal example

This view module creates a score label and its availability status. Put overcrow.js beside it. A null score remains visibly missing, and stale values keep their age.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Add ratings and reviews

FeaturePermissionService
Community scoreplayervox.score.readplayervox.score
Personal ratingplayervox.rating.readplayervox.rating
Rating editorplayervox.rating.writeplayervox.rating.requestEdit
Player reviewsplayervox.reviews.readplayervox.reviews
Followed-player filterplayervox.followed.read, plus reviews accessfollowedOnly: true

Each data service has snapshot() and onSnapshot(). All scores use 0–100. Community data includes the game name, ratings count and gameplay/art/tech criteria. A personal rating: null means no rating is available.

When a service reports notConnected, offer overcrow.playervox.requestConnect() from a button. To edit, call rating.requestEdit({expectedRevision}) using the current ready rating snapshot’s outer revision. OverCrow opens its editor; accepted does not mean saved or published.

reviews.page({page: 1, followedOnly: false}) requests a page; its data arrives through snapshots. Pages range from 1 to 1000 with up to 3 reviews each. Use totalPages to bound navigation. Preserve hidden: show a moderation notice instead of hidden review text, including its original version. Use translated and originalReview to distinguish translations; render text with textContent.

Rating, reviews and followed-player permissions are sensitive: no network or clipboard access, and browser data stays temporary even when storage is requested. Tokens and private account clients stay in OverCrow. Preview data is fictional; native connection/edit requests return cancelled.

Continue with shared service rules, the complete TypeScript definitions and the working reference widgets.

label: Journal
title: Read session history and open native actions
description: Browse local or cloud sessions, keep their source visible and request native edits.

blocks.html:
Build a session-history widget from the native journal. Each entry tells you when a session started, its duration and whether it came from local or cloud history.

Permissions

Merge these fields into your manifest for local history. Use journal.cloud.read for cloud history, or request both. Journal permissions are sensitive: no network or clipboard access, and browser data is temporary even when storage is requested.

blocks.title: manifest.json (fragment)

blocks.html:
Minimal example

This view module lists the current page and adds a next-page button. Put overcrow.js beside it. It preserves each session’s source and clears the list when data becomes unavailable.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Pages, notes and deletion

Pages contain at most 5 sessions. page({cursor: null}) requests the first page; pass nextCursor or previousCursor from current data for navigation. Treat cursors as opaque strings. A null cursor field means that direction is unavailable. The action returns a result; page contents arrive through snapshots.

durationMs is in milliseconds. Preserve source (local/cloud) and interrupted. endedAt and note can be null. Reading note text requires the separate journal.notes.read permission; a null note does not prove the user has never written one.

requestEditNote({sessionId, expectedRevision}) needs journal.notes.write and opens the native note editor. requestDelete({sessionId, expectedRevision}) needs journal.delete and opens native confirmation. Use the session ID and outer revision from the latest ready journal snapshot. An accepted result means opened or queued, not durably changed; never automatically replay an uncertain action.

For a cloud service reporting notConnected, offer overcrow.playervox.requestConnect() from a user-controlled button. Preview history is fictional and native edit/delete requests return cancelled. Temporary browser cleanup does not delete native journal records.

Continue with shared service rules, the complete TypeScript definitions and the working reference widgets.

label: Twitch
title: Read Twitch chat and open the message editor
description: Display messages through OverCrow’s shared connection and let the user compose natively.

headings.title: Let the user write or reply

blocks.html:
Display Twitch chat in your widget. To let someone write or reply, open OverCrow’s native message editor: the user types and confirms the message there.

Permissions

Merge these fields into your manifest. twitch.chat.read allows reading, connection and channel selection. This sensitive permission prohibits network and clipboard access and forces temporary browser data, even when storage is requested.

blocks.title: manifest.json (fragment)

blocks.html:
Minimal example

This view module displays the channel and messages as text. Put overcrow.js beside it. Each update replaces the previous display, including when access is lost.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Let the user write or reply

Add twitch.chat.compose to the capabilities for this optional module. A read-only widget cannot open the editor. The user types and confirms the message in OverCrow; the widget provides no text.

blocks.title: compose.js

blocks.html:
Connection, writing and replies

requestConnect() and requestChooseChannel() open native UI. All users follow the same native Twitch OAuth flow, shared by built-in and custom widgets. The initial connection requests user:read:chat and user:write:chat together. An existing connection authorized for both is reused; opening the editor needs no separate OAuth upgrade. These account scopes do not grant a widget permission to compose.

For a reply, use requestCompose({replyTo: message.id}) with an ID from current chat data. There is no send(text) or prefilled message body. Tokens, OAuth and direct Twitch connections stay native. An accepted result means opened or queued, not sent.

A snapshot holds at most 200 messages. Replace the displayed list on each update so deletions, clears and context changes remove old content. Render text as text. Optional reply information and text/emote fragments are described in the TypeScript definitions.

Emote handles work with overcrow.assets.read(handle): a local PNG Blob, at most 512 KiB. Revoke object URLs when finished; never substitute external URLs. Runtime, session or account changes discard temporary browser data. Preview chat is fictional; connect, channel-selection and compose requests return cancelled.

Continue with shared service rules, the complete TypeScript definitions and the working reference widgets.

label: Lifecycle
title: Lifecycle and messages
description: Keep state in a controller and react when the widget is hidden.

blocks.html: View or controller

blocks.title: Role set when the SDK loads
blocks.source: overcrow.runtime.role; // 'view', 'controller' or 'unavailable'

blocks.html:
Add "controller": "controller.html" to entrypoints for an optional controller. Both documents import the SDK. A plain browser reports unavailable; native calls reject.

Share a counter

The controller owns the count. A new view sends hello to receive its current value.

blocks.title: controller.js

blocks.html: Subscribe in the view before sending the first message:

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
send targets the other role. onMessage returns an unsubscribe function. To confirm that a message was processed, include a request ID and send a reply; the send promise alone confirms neither processing nor saving.

Messages must be plain JSON, at most 1 MiB and 64 levels deep. Functions, cycles, Date, Map, undefined and non-finite numbers are rejected.

Pause work when hidden

blocks.title: Visibility changes

blocks.html:
A hidden view may still have an active controller. Keep necessary state work running and pause unnecessary timers or animations.

Request a capture

await overcrow.surface.invalidate() asks OverCrow to refresh the surface. The runtime already observes page changes; reserve this call for a needed refresh rather than a continuous loop.

label: Storage
title: Save widget data
description: Read, write and remove local JSON data with overcrow.storage.

blocks.html:
Keep data between sessions

Use overcrow.storage to save JSON locally. OverCrow uses IndexedDB in storage isolated for each widget. To request persistence, add this to permissions in your manifest:

blocks.title: manifest.json · permissions
blocks.source: "storage": true

blocks.html:
Without this permission, or with sensitive capabilities, storage is temporary. The Studio and browser preview always use temporary memory, cleared when the preview reloads or its simulated game session changes.

Save and read JSON

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html: get() returns undefined for a missing key; a saved null stays null. set() completes after its transaction commits. Check whether a successful write is temporary or persistent:

blocks.title: Storage mode
blocks.source:
const { mode } = await overcrow.storage.getInfo();
console.log(mode); // 'persistent' or 'temporary'

blocks.html:
Limits and errors

ItemLimit
Keys256 keys; 1–128 UTF-8 bytes each.
ValuesJSON only; 64 KiB per value, 64 nesting levels.
Operations32 pending requests; opening and each transaction time out after 5 seconds.

Catch errors around awaited calls. On storage_quota_exceeded or storage_unavailable, keep the displayed data and report the failure. invalid_storage_key and invalid_storage_value indicate invalid inputs. Other codes are busy, invalid_response, stale_context and bridge_unavailable. An older host without this API returns unsupported; update OverCrow.

Protect saved work

  • Keep the widget ID stable. Validate and version stored documents; preserve unreadable data for recovery.
  • A separate get() then set() is not atomic. Centralize concurrent writes in the controller.
  • Persistence is not a backup. SDK data is not included in exported packages or Studio project drafts.

Existing localStorage/IndexedDB data is not migrated or deleted. Advanced IndexedDB use remains subject to the native policy; use a separate database, never overcrow.sdk.storage. Raw IndexedDB is unavailable in the online Studio. Never store credentials.

label: Languages
title: Widget languages
description: Use the OverCrow language preference with your translations.

blocks.html: Declare your languages

blocks.title: manifest.json fragment

blocks.html:
Declare 1–16 unique languages, including the default. Forms include fr, en and en-US. OverCrow uses an exact match for the Control Center preference, or the default otherwise.

Display translated text

Supply a dictionary for each language. Here both modules export an object with a ready label:

blocks.title: view.js · local dictionaries

blocks.html: Call stop() when removing the component. Without localization, getCurrent() returns null and no language-change event is emitted. You provide widget translations; marketplace listing translations are separate.

label: Clipboard
title: Copy to the clipboard
description: Copy prepared text from a click in interactive mode.

blocks.html: Declare the permission

blocks.title: Inside permissions
blocks.source: "clipboardWrite": true

blocks.html:
Copy on click

Prepare the text before the click and call writeText directly from the handler.

blocks.title: view.js

blocks.html:
Each current user gesture in interactive mode authorizes one write. Waiting for a network response can expire it. Text is limited to 16 KiB and cannot contain NUL.

Show the result

Show “Copied” only after success. On refusal, let the user retry. Test gestures in OverCrow; browser previews cannot validate them. The SDK supports writing, with no clipboard read access.

label: Test
title: Test your widget
description: Inspect the native engine, replay events and test the game overlay.

blocks.html: Test with the creator kit

blocks.title: From a creator-kit project
blocks.source: npm run dev -- --native --devtools

blocks.html:
The kit validates sources, recalculates hashes and reloads the native view. The controller keeps running; restart after changing its code. Use this offscreen session for engine checks. Import a package to test the game overlay. For layout, use the kit and its reloading browser preview.

Use the Linux CLI

Build your framework if necessary, then prepare its static output and register that output with the native CLI. Permissions remain explicit; use a fresh private output directory for each preparation.

blocks.title: Linux · output parent must be private (0700)
blocks.source:
mkdir -m 700 /absolute/path/output
overcrow-widget prepare /absolute/path/dist /absolute/path/output/build-1
overcrow-widget dev --watch --devtools /absolute/path/output/build-1

blocks.html: Reload a prepared folder

blocks.title: File notification reload
blocks.source: overcrow-widget dev --watch /absolute/path/widget

blocks.html:
The watcher groups edit bursts and accepts only consistent manifest and hashes. Invalid changes keep the last valid view and controller. Run your framework build yourself. Use npm run dev -- --native to recalculate hashes automatically.

Expanded permissions stop the session with capability_confirmation_required. Review the new manifest and start a fresh registration.

Load from a local server

blocks.title: Server must supply consistent manifest and files
blocks.source: overcrow-widget dev --url http://127.0.0.1:4173

blocks.html:
Use a numeric loopback address and explicit port; localhost is not accepted. The host downloads and freezes verified files. The widget does not connect directly to the server; this is not an HMR or WebSocket tunnel. --watch cannot be combined with --url.

Replay test events

blocks.title: Creator kit · Windows and Linux
blocks.source: npm run dev -- --native --replay ./events.json

blocks.title: events.json · example fixture
Declare event in permissions.gameEvents
blocks.source: overcrow-widget dev --watch --replay /absolute/path/events.json /absolute/path/widget

blocks.html:
Events follow file order, with non-decreasing timestamps. Limits are 1 MiB and 1,024 events. Replay runs again after a successful reload. Here elapsedMs is a fixture field, not the native snapshot's sessionElapsedMs.

Inspect errors

--devtools opens local developer tools. The terminal reports replacement failures; the inspector shows engine details. Console output can contain private data. Remove tokens and personal responses before sharing a report.

label: Distribute
title: Distribute a widget
description: Export a package and prepare its marketplace listing.

blocks.html:
Before export

  • Test small sizes, zoom, passive and interactive modes.
  • Handle loading, empty data, failure and recovery.
  • Check saving and returning after the view is hidden.
  • Include every local resource and license in the prepared bundle.

Build a package

Run npm run package in a Windows/Linux creator-kit project. The command prints the output path and recalculates hashes. See the complete flow. With the Linux native CLI:

blocks.title: Linux · writes .ocpkg beside the folder
blocks.source: overcrow-widget package /absolute/path/prepared-widget

blocks.html:
The command validates manifest and files and creates a deterministic stored ZIP with the .ocpkg extension. It neither signs nor installs nor publishes. Changes to bytes require re-preparation, and each new published widget version needs a new version number.

Prepare a listing

listing.json describes the author, license, source and catalog translations. It is separate from runtime files. Listing translations do not declare languages actually supplied by the widget.

Read the marketplace creator guide ↗ and review policy ↗.

Marketplace screenshot. Add a PNG to your widget, for example widget/preview.png, before preparing its package. In the publication sidecar listing.json, set "preview": "preview.png" or another relative path such as "preview": "images/screenshot.png". The image must appear in the generated manifest.files ledger. Use a static PNG of at most 256 KiB and 1,024 × 1,024 pixels; 960 × 600 is a useful landscape format. URLs, SVGs, animated images and paths outside the widget are rejected.

The marketplace displays the admitted image on cards and detail pages, with a neutral placeholder if it is absent. Changing a published screenshot requires a new widget version and signed publication.

Review and installation

Review and publication use the validated listing, manifest and exact package bytes. The signed catalog and installation consent are separate from local development. “Open in OverCrow” opens a listing in Control Center; it does not install or activate a widget automatically.

Licenses

The SDK and examples here are MIT-licensed; keep their notices. They do not force you to license your own widget under MIT. The public policy for admitting third-party licenses is still pending; successful format validation alone does not authorize publication.

label: Troubleshooting
title: Troubleshooting
description: Find an error and the next step to try.

blocks.html:
Error codes

Symptom / codeLikely causeNext step
bridge_unavailableThe SDK cannot find the native runtime.Use dev or an installed package; a plain web server has no native bridge.
invalid_manifest / invalid_bundle / invalid widget projectSchema, path, file or hash is inconsistent.Check entrypoints and permissions, then prepare a fresh output.
unsafe_pathRelative path, symlink or incompatible permissions.Use a real absolute path and private 0700 output parent.
capability_confirmation_requiredReload requests more permissions.Review the change and explicitly restart development.
capability_denied / permission_deniedPermission or current user gesture is missing or expired.Check manifest and consent; click again in interactive mode for clipboard.
body_usedThe same response body was read twice.Read json(), text() or arrayBuffer() once and store the result.
invalid_message / message_too_largeMessage is not small, plain JSON.Avoid cycles and split large application data.
request_body_limitRequest body exceeds 2 MiB.Reduce the request or split it if the API permits.
busy / unresponsiveOperation overlaps or runtime did not respond in time.Disable duplicate actions, then offer a retry.
Blank view after an editJavaScript error, missing entrypoint or unprepared build.Open devtools, check index.html and prepare again.
Session events do not fireDeclaring a name does not create a live feed.Use onSnapshot for native updates; check replay event names/payloads.
HTTP 4xx / 5xxRemote service refused or failed.Check response.ok, show an error and retain last valid data.

Check three things

  1. Does the HTML render with local assets at the expected size?
  2. Is the widget running in OverCrow with required permissions?
  3. Does received data match the schema your code expects?

Report an issue

Include OverCrow, widget and SDK versions; platform; minimal steps; expected versus actual result; and error code. Use a small example or non-personal fixture. Application diagnostics can prepare a report for explicit submission.

Runtime limits

The SDK has no shell, Node, Tauri, arbitrary file access or game-memory reading. External browser network access is blocked. An invented manifest permission cannot open those boundaries.
